cohort: The study included 5231 weighted samples of women who delivered in health facilities in Ghana, drawn from the 2022 DHS datasets.
finding: The prevalence of caesarean section (CS) in Ghana was 20.29%, which is higher than the WHO recommended level, and was significantly associated with maternal age, education, wealth, employment, parity, age at first birth, pregnancy type, birth size, birth weight, and geographical region.
mod_finding: The rate of caesarean section delivery in Ghana was 20.29%, and it was significantly associated with maternal age, education, wealth, employment, parity, age at first birth, multiple pregnancy, large birth size, 4-6 kg birth weight, and specific regions.
